Fixed the two remaining pool-bake defects from the "spurious first-boot `mngr stop`" investigation (mngr-internal issue #775) -- both proved to be the bake's own finalize sequence, not a tmux race:

- The bake now waits for the whole default-workspace-template env-converge slow phase (env.d units including the Fortress/Chromium install, environment-record capture, and the rootfs stamp) to finish before parking the services agent, instead of waiting only for the Fortress binary -- which a cached image can already carry while apt is still running. Previously the park could kill env-converge mid-run, shipping baked slices without `apt.json` or the rootfs stamp. The wait completes on the rootfs stamp, bails early when supervisord reports the one-shot EXITED/FATAL (or unknown), and still proceeds with a warning on timeout (the converge retries on lease). `--skip-deferred-install-wait` keeps its name and now skips this broader wait.

- After the park, the bake now verifies that the baked container holds only the primary services agent (via in-container `mngr list --format json`) and fails the bake loudly -- rolling the slice VM back -- on any non-primary agent, an untrustworthy listing (command failure, unparseable output, discovery errors), or an empty listing. This replaces the trust that the historical chat teardown earned nothing: its wrong-name `mngr destroy --force` silently missed the bootstrap `Chat-1` agent for weeks. Old default-workspace-template tags whose bootstrap still creates a boot chat are deliberately refused by this check; bake a tag without a boot chat instead.
